page:library.text: Your library, your secrets. Archive what you don't need. Delete what could hang you.
And keep the drafts. Every good plan starts as a bad note.
Characters, rides, contacts, notes. A whole life in one list. Mine's shorter.
Yours is shorter because you keep deleting the evidence, Nine.
Start a new one. Fresh face, fresh SIN, fresh mistakes.
Same old mistakes, actually. Faster this time.

page:catalog.text: Window shopping. The only shopping that doesn't leave a paper trail.
Pretty sure the catalog's watching you back.
Every gun in the book and not one in my size.
They make 'em in your size, Mule. They're called vehicle mounts.
Check the page number before you argue with your GM. Saves a fist-fight.

page:account.text: Change your password like you change your safehouse: before you need to.
And log out everywhere when the van starts smelling funny.
Easier font on? Smart. Reading the fine print kept me alive twice.
The fine print is where the corps hide the knives.
New theme. Same shadows. Feels better though.
Green on black for nostalgia. Pink on black for style.

page:admin.text: Sysop's console. Every invite is a door. Count your doors.
And close the ones nobody walks through.
Make a second admin before you need one. Ask me how I learned.
Locked myself out for a week. Ate a lot of soy.
Fence or refund, the sysop decides. The runners complain either way.

page:help.text: Reading the manual. Respect. Most runners learn by bleeding.
If the help doesn't help, file an issue. Politely. Sysops remember tone.
And say which page broke. 'It's broken' is a riddle, not a report.
Page numbers in every answer. Take them to your GM like a lawyer.

page:sign-in.text: Invite only. If you're reading this, somebody vouched for you. Don't make them regret it.
Handle and password. Nothing else. No names, no faces.
Forgot your password? Ask your sysop for a reset. Don't ask me, I don't even know mine.
Reset links work once. Like most good ideas.
Jack in, chummer. The board's been quiet.

page:character.text: Every number on that sheet is a decision somebody's going to test with a gun.
Or a spell. Don't forget the spells.
Check the Rules box before you finish. The book doesn't forgive and neither does your GM.
My GM forgives. Then she remembers. Then she sends a dragon.
A runner's history is a list of debts. Read yours before you sell anything.
And undo is not a lifestyle.

page:vehicle.text: Hardpoints for the big guns, firmpoints for the polite ones.
Cargo space is where good plans go to rust. Pack light.
Link it, don't buy it, until you know you'll keep it.

page:workshop.text: Design Points don't lie. The salesman does.
Mark-Up is where the salesman lives.
Built a hovercraft once. It handled like a shopping cart full of grenades.
That was the point, as I recall.
Drive-by-wire: when your car trusts your brain more than you do.
Mine never trusted my brain. Smart car.

page:npc.text: Every contact has a price and a breaking point. Write down both.
Professional ones don't break. They just invoice you.
Twenty-five years in the business and still bouncing. That's experience.
A Threat Rating is the GM's way of saying 'this one's read the manual too'.
My Threat Rating is 'large'. Works on most people.

page:draft.text: Notes. The only thing more dangerous than a plan is a plan written down.
So write it here, not on a napkin in a bar.
Revision history. Even your mistakes get a timestamp.

page:any.text: Mind your manners too. Sysop's watching.
Rain again. Of course it's raining.
It's Seattle, Rusty. It's always raining.
Puddles reflect neon. Free light show.
Anybody got work? Asking for a friend. The friend is me.
Fixer on 3rd is hiring. Bring your own body bag.
Heard the Stuffer Shack on 5th has real coffee now.
Heard wrong. It's soykaf with brown dye.
Reminder: the board never sleeps, but you should.
Sleep is for people without drain headaches.
